items.title: Water Jug - Whiteware, Red, Transfer-printed, England, Staffordshire,1842-1862 (Fragment)
items.summary: This ceramic water pitcher has been reconstructed from a group of fragments that were excavated at one of the digs on the Commonwealth Block between 1988 and 2003. The pattern is known as 'Panama'. It is one of a pair. Uncovering past food practices. Of all the archaeological material uncovered in the Little Lon excavations, the remnants of eating and drinking are the most numerous. Broken plates, bowls, cups and cutlery were thrown into rubbish piles with smashed jars that once held jam and pickles, and jugs that held water or cordial. Shells from oysters, abalone and coconuts were tossed in with bones from mutton, beef, rabbit and pork. Pips and seeds from fruit and vegetables were also added to the piles. These objects offer clues to the food consumed by residents of Little Lon, and are important in the rediscovery of a people, place and time long vanished.

items.title: Apple Model - Royal Russet, Burnley, 1874
items.summary: This wax model is based on a specimen grown by the Horticultural Society of Victoria at their Burnley gardens and the model presented to the museum by the National Agricultural Society in 1874 after the specimen was exhibited at the National Agricultural Society's Show, 3-5 April 1873. The model was made in the museum by Thomas McMillan in 1873 for the National Agricultural Society. See also Reg Item 013571 and 013572. Synonyms: Leather Coat, Reinette de Canada Grise, Reinette de Canada Platte, Rousette Royale. This apple is a cooking variety and is harvested in autumn-winter.

items.title: Leaflets - Matmaking Machines Specifications & Instructions, circa 1950s-1980s
items.summary: Folder of documents containing guidelines for the installation and service of the Thorvald Clasen trimming machine and sharpener, circa 1950s-1980s. Some are from the manufacturer and others are from previous owners of the machines. These machines were used at the matmaking workshop at the Royal Victorian Institute for the Blind from 1986 until it closed down in 1992. The Trimming machine was previously used to make mats at Pentridge Prison.

It was used in Footscray, Victoria, Australia, circa 1946-1992. ; the sugar bowl and milk jug were made by Keele Street Pottery Co. Ltd, design style 845007, registered in 1945.

items.title: Loom - Countermarch Floor Loom, Germany, circa 1945
items.summary: Countermarch floor loom made for Anna Apinis by fellow survivors of World War II, in Memmingen, a displaced persons camp in Germany with wood scavenged from bombed-out ruins. It was designed by Anna's husband Ervins. Anna used the loom to weave traditional Latvian designs using threads gathered by unraveling old scraps of fabric. Anna brought the loom with her to Australia and continued to weave Latvian designs on it.

items.title: Sandals - Paragon, Belle Chaussure, 'Corso', Gold, Olive & Light Green, 1983
items.summary: Pair of sandals with striped panels of strips of leather in gold, olive and light green. Low stacked Cuban heel, cross-over vamp, open toe and ankle strap uppers. Part of the Belle Chaussure, 'Corso' range, made in 1983 by Paragon. These sandals were worn by the donor. Paragon Shoes Pty Ltd was one of the most significant 20th century Australian shoe retailers, and at one time was the largest manufacturer of high quality of women's shoes in Australia. Its factory was located in Melbourne, and its shoes were sold throughout Australia and New Zealand.
